idea-plugin.name: Kensington
idea-plugin.description:
CSS class name completions and validation for the Kensington JS template engine.

Completion

Autocomplete triggers inside { class: '...' } and { class: ['...'] } expressions in JavaScript and TypeScript files. Multiple classes in one string are handled correctly — completion applies only to the word being typed, not the whole value.

Class names are sourced from:

  • Local files — all .css, .scss, and .less files in the project.
  • CDN stylesheets — any https://…​.css URL found in HTML, CSS, SCSS, Less, JS, or TS files (including <link href="…">, CSS @import url("…"), and Kensington t.link({ href: '…' }) calls). CDN files are fetched in the background, cached for 24 hours, and refreshed automatically when a relevant file is saved. Commented-out URLs are ignored.

Unknown class inspection

Class names that don't exist in any local or CDN stylesheet are highlighted with a warning. Two quick fixes are available via Alt+Enter:

  • Ignore class '…' — suppresses the warning for that specific class name permanently. The ignored list is saved in the project's inspection profile and can be viewed and edited in Settings → Editor → Inspections → Kensington → Unknown CSS class → Ignored Classes.
  • Disable 'Unknown CSS class' inspection — turns off the inspection for the whole project. A Re-enable link appears in the notification that follows. The inspection can also be re-enabled at any time in Settings → Editor → Inspections → Kensington.
